metadata.hardware_requirements: computing server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores)

nodes_source.source_quote: A series of simulation experiments based on real-world traffic data are conducted to evaluate the proposed approach.
nodes_source.description: Traffic volume data from a freeway segment connecting Qingdao and Huangdao in Shandong, China. It includes 10-minute traffic volumes from 7:50 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. for the mainline and on-ramp.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: The paper's Data Availability section explicitly states the data are available from the corresponding author upon request.

nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices.
nodes_process.description: Extract vehicle locations (xi, yi) from raw video frames within a control area (X by Y) and encode them into a position matrix containing binary location data and signal states.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, tool generically described but procedure explicitly detailed in eq (3)-(5).

nodes_process.source_quote: Three consecutive observations are stacked to represent the traffic state.
nodes_process.description: Down-sample individual position matrices to size 4 by 512 and stack three consecutive time steps (N=3) to create the input tensor for the deep Q-network.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all stacking and dimensionality parameters stated in text and Table 1.

nodes_process.source_quote: A multitask learning strategy is implemented in the training process to improve learning efficiency.
nodes_process.description: Train a three-layer CNN with Adam to optimize a dual loss: Q-value estimation (L1) and prediction of mean speed and queue length (L2) using experience replay and a frozen target network.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, hardware and all Table 1 hyperparameters specified for training.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator.
nodes_process.description: Simulate 20 trials for three scenarios (No control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL) on the Qingdao-Huangdao freeway tunnel model from 7:50 AM to 9:00 AM.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, simulator named and setup parameters given, trial counts defined.

nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data.
nodes_process.description: Partition the control area into eight subareas and systematically remove visual information from each to measure impact on mainline travel times.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, methodology for perturbing subareas is fully specified with clear result reporting.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2 presents mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments. It is found that the performance of the PI-ALINEA method is not always better than that of the no-control scenario.
nodes_sink.description: Mean vehicle travel times in seconds for 20 distinct simulation experiments, comparing No-control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL scenarios including percentage differences.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Hyperparameters and method are specified, but specific SUMO network files and raw traffic demand profiles are not public.

nodes_sink.source_quote: The episode reward and mean travel time are both converged in 400,000 training frames and can maintain a stable value until the end of the training process.
nodes_sink.description: Two convergence plots showing episode reward and mean travel time during the DRL training process up to 1 million frames.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: DRL architecture (Fig 7) and hyperparameters (Tab 1) are well-documented; training procedure uses standard tools (Adam, GPU/CPU spec).

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Distributions of vehicle travel times in the mainline freeway section from 8:00 to 9:00 AM across No-control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Method follows directly from SUMO simulation outputs based on described setups, though source traffic demand data is not provided via URL.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 10 presents the temporal-spatial distribution of the mean speeds along the mainline. The results further demonstrate the efficiency of the ramp metering.
nodes_sink.description: Heatmaps displaying temporal-spatial speed distribution along a 4000m stretch of mainline for No-control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL cases.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: While visual outcome is clear, exact cell bin sizes for the spatio-temporal map calculation are not explicitly specified.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: On-ramp vehicle queue lengths (m) from 8:00 to 9:00 AM for three scenarios, showing interquartile ranges.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: SUMO queue extraction is standard; parameters for controllers are clearly stated in previous sections.

nodes_sink.source_quote: The better performance of the proposed DRL method is further revealed when considering traffic flows downstream of the merge area, which is demonstrated in Figure 14.
nodes_sink.description: Box plots of downstream volume (veh/h) across thirteen time bins for three control strategies.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Consistent with previously described simulation evaluation metrics and statistical reporting.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed, and the baseline is the result of experiments that take original data as input.
nodes_sink.description: Box plots showing sensitivity analysis of mainline travel time when input from specific camera subareas is removed from the DRL agent.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Procedure involves mask-based perturbation which is partially described but exact mask implementation detail is brief.
